newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins dip on profit-taking, seen lower.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins dip on profit-taking, seen lower.

text.p: Profit taking pushed down prices of Russian MinFin bonds by about 0.4 points on Monday, dealers said, forecasting the trend to cash in on recent historic gains would continue through the week.
Dealers said the most actively traded fourth and fifth tranches could ease to around 67.00-67.50 and 49.00-49.50 respectively by Friday.
"It is a normal situation when a correction starts after a strong rise and stabilisation," an ICFI Moscow Partners Bank dealer said.

"The market has risen too high, there is nothing to push prices up," one dealer said. He said Westerners who had built up large positions recently had begun selling. Western banks had actively sold 2003 and 2008 maturities.
"Besides, profits are being taken on U.S. Treasuries as well," the dealer said.

MinFins set records in early July when the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) left interest rates unchanged at a regular meeting. Prices had set new consecutive records for a week until last Wednesday, when profit-taking set in.
MinFins, along with other emerging market debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
Dealers said trading was to some extent thinner because of the Bastille Day holiday in France.
They added the market was unaffected by news that Russia expected a delay in the announcement of the closing agreement with the London Club of commercial bank creditors.
Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov said Russia will further delay the announcement of the closing agreement by a period of less than one month.
